newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila sets test on seaweed as food additive.
newsitem.headline: Manila sets test on seaweed as food additive.

text.p: The Philippine Bureau of Fisheries and Aquatic Resources said on Thursday it had signed an agreement with local seaweed growers to fund a test on the safety of seaweed-based carrageenan as a food additive.

The joint programme between the state agency and the Seaweed Industry Association of the Philippines was intended to provide scientific data and prove the non-toxicity of the seaweed-based, Philippine natural grade carrageenan as a food additive, it said in a statement.
The study could be used to help the Philippines penetrate more markets in Europe and the United States.
Under the plan, the government will fund a "toxicology" study on carrageenan by an internationally recognised laboratory.
The Philippines sold $98.343 million worth of semi-refined and refined carrageenan in Southeast Asia, Australia, New Zealand, Africa, Middle East, Japan, the United States and Europe in 1995.
The material is used as a stabiliser in a range of products including toothpaste, ice cream, dairy and personal care products.
